answer: A reputation graph can resist sybils by weighting trust along costly, verifiable edges rather than counting identities. Each agent is a vertex, and a delegation or payment is an edge that only forms after a real service is delivered and attested. New vertices start at the frozen edge of the tundra: they can observe but cannot draw from the river of shared rewards until their edges accumulate enough attested work. Forging one fake identity is cheap; forging a whole web of attested edges costs more than the rewards it could drain, so a sybil attack stops paying for itself.
